newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus targets higher 1997 grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus targets higher 1997 grain harvest.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Belarus is predicting a grain harvest of 6.5 million tonnes this year compared to 5.8 million tonnes in 1996, the deputy chief of the Agriculture Ministry's crop division said on Wednesday.
"This year we have expanded the sowing area on collective farms and state farms to 2.6 million hectares, against 2.58 million hectares last year," Vyacheslav Herasimovich told Reuters.
"Including private plots, there will be 2.70 to 2.75 million hectares sown to grain," he said, adding that sowing had started in the southern Gomel and Brest regions where warm conditions prevailed.
Herasimovich said winter grain was generally in good condition and re-sowing would not be necessary.
He said the government had advanced 3.3 trillion Belarussian roubles to pre-purchase 50 percent of the 1997 grain harvest and 30 percent of the sugar beet and flax harvest.
Herasimovich said an early spring was not bringing consistently high temperatures, making it impossible to predict when sowing would start in earnest or when it would finish.
"Unfortunately we can already forecast that there will not be enough moisture in the spring and summer because there was little snow this winter," he said.

Herasimovich added Belarus planned to use 30 percent more fertiliser this year than last, but said the largest threat to the harvest was severe fuel shortages, with only seven percent of diesel and eight percent of the necessary gas available.
"I think that the situation will be corrected since the government has issued a 500 billion Belarussian rouble trade credit to buy fuel," he said.
President Alexander Lukashenko has also extended a tax-free open credit line of two trillion roubles to the agricultural sector.
